structured.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: The smallest country in the Western Hemisphere by both area and population, Saint Kitts and Nevis consists of two volcanic islands in the Caribbean Sea, separated by a 3-km-wide channel called The Narrows. Baseball-bat-shaped Saint Kitts has the Great Salt Pond at its southern tip, while ball-shaped Nevis is dominated by Nevis Peak at its center. It has no land borders with any country.
prose.physicalGeography: Saint Kitts and Nevis lies in the Caribbean Sea, roughly a third of the way between Puerto Rico and Trinidad and Tobago. Both islands are volcanic with mountainous interiors.
prose.climate: The climate is tropical but tempered by constant sea breezes, with little seasonal temperature variation. A rainy season runs from May to November, and hurricanes are a risk from July to October. Mount Liamuiga (1,156 m) on Saint Kitts and Nevis Peak (985 m) on Nevis are both part of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles, which stretches from Saba in the north to Grenada in the south.
prose.economy: This is a high-income, tourism-based economy within the Caribbean OECS, and the country belongs to both CARICOM and the ECCU. It has been building a growing offshore financial and telecommunications sector alongside a distinctive citizenship-driven growth model, though the economy remains environmentally fragile. Key industries include tourism, cotton, salt, copra, clothing, footwear, and beverages, while exports include ships, measuring instruments, beer, electrical transformers, and electrical control boards.
prose.peopleAndCulture: English is the official language. The population is predominantly of African descent (92.5%), with smaller mixed (3%), White (2.1%), and East Indian (1.5%) communities.
